correctness.rationale: The exact finite generator on the observable basis (1,n1,n2,n1n2) factorizes as \(z(z+a+b)[z^2+(a+b+2h)z+ab+h(a+b)]\). Because h>0, only z=-(a+b) can collide, precisely if \(h(a+b)=ab\). The (a,-b) mean eigenvector couples into joint occupancy with \(ab(q-p)\), so geometric multiplicity is one iff p differs from q; otherwise it is two. Integrating the forced pair equation produces the exact polynomial-times-exponential amplitude. The extracted standalone verify.py passed symbolic identities, exact rational Jordan ranks, and 30 independent matrix-exponential comparisons. The proof, not a finite sample, covers the full stated positive-parameter domain.

originality.rationale: The source 2026 spectrum-invariance theorem already covers density-independent eigenvalues and exhibits a defective three-site example; the present classification instead identifies the iff two-site parameter surface, the non-equilibrium Jordan condition, minimality and a joint-observable signature invisible to means. The 2019 integrable eigenvector construction explicitly assumes nondegenerate eigenvalues; the 2023 stationary-law analysis does not supply a transient exceptional-point theorem. Actual targeted published-result and literature searches revealed no direct or dominating equivalent. Publication priority remains qualified because a finite-matrix special case or a previously published integrability extension may have been overlooked.
residual_risks: A simple two-site exceptional-point classification may appear as a special case in unpublished notes, integrability appendices or earlier finite-chain spectral studies not located by the finite searches.

The theorem is intentionally about the smallest two-site system; broader nonequilibrium networks may exhibit qualitatively different exceptional loci.

value.rationale: The smallest physically realizable boundary-driven exclusion channel has a sharply specified nonequilibrium defective-generator surface, not merely a repeated spectral root. The theorem separates reservoir-density-independent eigenvalues from reservoir-density-dependent Jordan structure, and proves an experimentally observable joint-occupancy polynomial-times-exponential term while every individual occupancy mean stays a sum of exponentials. This clarifies how real-spectrum nonequilibrium chains can hide slow polynomial prefactors from common measurements and provides a complete exact benchmark for higher-dimensional spectral questions.
